nodes.name: Tropical rainfall
nodes.desc: Heavy rain on the Caribbean slope feeds the rivers, lagoons and wet forest of the reserve.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Year-round warmth and light let the rainforest canopy grow in several layers.

nodes.name: Río Plátano floods
nodes.desc: The river and its lagoons carry water and silt through the lowlands and shape the wetlands and gallery forest.

nodes.name: Forest soil & litter
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and soil hold nutrients that plants take up again.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, wood, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Ice-cream bean
nodes.desc: A leguminous tree whose fruit pulp is eaten by many bats, birds and monkeys, per GloBI feeding records.

nodes.name: Cocoplum
nodes.desc: A coastal and wetland shrub whose fruit is eaten by bats and fruit-eating birds in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Miconia
nodes.desc: A genus of shrubs common in the secondary growth; berries are taken by bats and tanagers.

nodes.name: Davilla liana
nodes.desc: A woody climber whose fruits feed a range of birds in GloBI feeding records.

nodes.name: Jamaican fruit bat
nodes.desc: A common fruit bat among the best-recorded mammals here; it eats fruit and so spreads seeds.

nodes.name: Desmarest's spiny pocket mouse
nodes.desc: A forest-floor rodent that eats seeds and fruit and is prey for cats, snakes and hawks.

nodes.name: Black-handed spider monkey
nodes.desc: A canopy fruit-eater listed as a reserve primate; GloBI records it eating Inga fruit.

nodes.name: Mantled howler
nodes.desc: A leaf and fruit eater of the canopy and a documented resident of the reserve.

nodes.name: Baird's tapir
nodes.desc: A large browser of leaves and twigs in wet forest and swamp. Adults have few natural predators besides jaguars and big crocodiles.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: A pig-like forest forager and a regular prey of large cats.

nodes.name: Scarlet macaw
nodes.desc: Eats fruit, nuts, seeds and flowers. The reserve is noted for its macaws.

nodes.name: Montezuma oropendola
nodes.desc: A well-recorded colonial bird; GloBI shows it eating cocoplum, Davilla and coral-bean fruit.

nodes.name: Terciopelo
nodes.desc: A large pit viper that eats small mammals and other vertebrates; GloBI records it eating a coffee snake.

nodes.name: Roadside hawk
nodes.desc: A common small hawk that hunts lizards, small mammals and other prey.

nodes.name: Ocelot
nodes.desc: A spotted cat on the reserve's threatened list that hunts small mammals on the forest floor.

nodes.name: Black vulture
nodes.desc: One of the most-recorded birds near the reserve; it scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Harpy eagle
nodes.desc: A huge forest eagle named among the reserve's birds. It hunts monkeys and sloths in the canopy.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: Apex cat of the reserve. It takes peccaries, deer and sometimes tapirs.
